quotes:
`instance_lifecycle`'s two listeners share one HTTP implementation. Each
connection's socket waits at most the imported
`LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (30) for the next bytes of a request — its
headers or its body, an upload's head and file among them; a wait that
reaches it ends the stream with a failure, which the reader sees as any
stream failure: an upload's head then gives no CSRF value (refused at stage
(1)), its file part `file_unreadable`, and the connection is closed. A
request answered before its body was read to its framed end — any request,
not an upload alone — has the remainder discarded unread and its
connection closed; a connection carries a next request only after one whose
body was read to its end.
judgement.why: State 6 applies the timeout to both listeners' shared HTTP implementation and to the socket waits for request headers and bodies, including upload heads and files and the headers of a subsequent request.

One response in that wire format, v1's (owner, 2026-11-17): the answer, or
the refusal's code, stage and kinds. An answer is written as its fields with
no `answer_kind` or `view_kind` on the wire; `validate` and `context` are
their v1 bodies, field for field (R0-04). Instants are ISO 8601 text in UTC
ending in `Z`, dates ISO 8601 dates, decimals JSON strings in the stored form
(`"45.00"`). The HTTP status is the imported `SERVICE_ANSWER_STATUS` for an
answer and, for a refusal, its code's in the imported
`REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES` — v1's: `not_found` 404, `internal_error` 500, every
other code 422.

None of its own: it refuses nothing. An operation name that is not one of
A09 rule 2's reaches `operations`, which refuses it at stage (1) as outside
the service's rights (`not_permitted`, `outside_service_rights`), whatever
token it carries once the token is valid; inputs that are not of the wire
format — a body that cannot be read as it, a field it does not declare, a
value of another shape than its field's — are answered stage (1) first and
then `invalid_request` (`outside_closed_list`) at stage (4).
judgement.why: State 6 makes expiry a stream failure visible to the reader, maps upload-head and upload-file failures, and requires closing the connection; State 5 already fixes the service refusal and its HTTP status when a body cannot be read as the wire format.
